title: Bramley and rhubarb pots with hazelnut crunch

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Bramleys, rhubarb, orange, sugar, cinnamon, nuts, seeds, butter, honey and natural yoghurt are all ordinary home kitchen foods.

supermarket.reason: Everything, including the hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds, is on everyday Tesco shelves at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It only needs a saucepan, frying pan, grater and bowls, and the techniques are simple stewing and toasting.

works.reason: About 700g of fruit with a little water and orange juice will cook down to a thick compote in 10 to 12 minutes, which is a generous four portions with 400g of yoghurt, and the honeyed crunch balances the sharpness.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and chopping two Bramleys, cutting the rhubarb, zesting, chopping nuts and toasting fits in about 20 minutes, and 45 minutes total covers cooking and 20 minutes of cooling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps under its true name, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early April rhubarb with stored Bramleys is right for the date, and the fruit compote is the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and friendly, written in plain British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, natural yoghurt and nuts with only a little added sugar make a satisfying, wholesome afternoon snack.
